utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So good afternoon. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, this is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. All the accused are here. Prosecution Mr. McCloskey, the Defence teams, I notice the absence of Mr. Bourgon. Yes, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to all of my learned friends. I want to introduce our new associate, our assistant Ms. Marie-Josee Barry-Gosselin from Canada who will be working with the Nikolic defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome. You are most welcome. So absent is Mr. Bourgon, Mr. Sarapa, and I think that's it. All right. Before we start, this is a nice occasion, the second -- for the second time that I'm happy to announce that another member of the Defence teams, namely David Josse, has, like previously Mr. Haynes, now been awarded the Queen's Counsel distinction. Our sincere congratulations to you, Mr. Josse. It's a well-deserved recognition of your distinguished career so far, and in a way, I also look at it as a recognition on the part of the authorities in the United Kingdom that bestowed this distinction of the work British or UK lawyers have been doing in this Tribunal. Yes, Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Just to say, Your Honours, I'm sure that is right. I'm personally very glad that this is becoming a habit, and I'm embarrassed and grateful for the kind words of the Trial Chamber. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So Mr. Zivanovic, and good afternoon to you, and good afternoon to you, Mr. Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, while giving evidence, you saw the Prosecution Exhibit 302. This is a piece of construction machinery ULT 220. Can we please look at the exhibit? This is a digger, an excavator. The copy is somewhat pale, the B/C/S, but I believe you've seen the document before, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed I have. In my understanding, this is a loader, and it cannot really be used as an excavator to quite the same extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see that excavator is one of the terms used in the translation. I'm not trying to discuss the particular type right now, but can we please go to the next page of this work log. Would you please look at the second entry, the date is the 17th of July. Do you agree with me that what it says is that the machine was used in Branjevo on that day; right?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we please go back to page 1 now. Can we please look at the fuel receipt information and the types specified there. You will see for the 17th of July, I think what it says is 100 litres were received at first and then another 70; am I right?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we, therefore, agree that this is not fuel that was poured over from some jerrycans or anything like that, this was one of those regular powers done at a petrol station; right?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a possibility that the machine went directly to the petrol station and got petrol there, got its fuel there; but it may have been issued in barrels as well, and then the barrels were taken to the place where the machine itself was waiting. I can't really tell which of the two was, in fact, the case. I see that the signatures of the handlers are quite different.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the person who actually issued the fuel?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But there was a different document based on which the fuel was issued?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a vehicle work log.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you're quite right, but if you look at column 2, fuel issued there is a document number?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the same document?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's probably the same document, no distinction being drawn based on how the fuel was delivered in barrels or whether someone went there and got it. This is something that they had to record at the petrol station and draft the appropriate document indicating that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You can see the number of the document 21/3-667 that's also recorded on the face of this document, right, you agree with that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that in the translation, but we can't see the actual figure in the original document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the date the document bears the date the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time any fuel was received for this piece of machine was in the 15th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Based on this document; right?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on this document, yes, and that's when the machine was first used. It wasn't part of the military stock, and it want recorded on the lists. It was borrowed in a way in Glinica company on that very day not having previously been mobilised for a military purpose. The driver or whoever operated the machine, and as it happens it was Veljko Kovacevic was not a man whose name was on the list of the engineering company.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Nevertheless, I'm looking at this document, the 15th of July. The fuel was issued twice on the 15th of July and according to the same document on the 17th of July as well. Do you agree that that's what it says?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree. If you look at other vehicle work logs, you might find the same document number there as well. It's got an entire page there, and there can be several entries in relation to the individual times at which fuel was issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: My impression is that this is not the same document as the one from the materiel list dated the 16th of July, the one that you looked at.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not the same document, that is the problem, isn't it? Or rather not a problem, it's actually a solution to the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What about the document numbers, are they the same? Are there any differences between the documents? If you want, we can compare them directly and see if there are any discrepancies.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the yesterday's number. I can't stretch my memory that far back, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not forging ahead with this, but I would like to go to another exhibit that you've seen already, OTP Exhibit 297. This is the daily order log of the engineering company of the Zvornik Brigade. You looked at page 134 of this document and now can we please go to 137. In the English, it's page 17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'd just like to -- is there a new list of documents because everything that's been produced today is not on the existing list by the Popovic Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic, only you can clear this up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This particular document was used in the examination-in-chief. This document, this book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Haynes does that satisfy you?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, we'll muddle along. I don't think it satisfies the rule let alone me but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a daily order concerning of the work of the engineering company in relation to the 17th of July, 1995. You agree, don't you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Right there in the middle of the page, in bold, you have the word "tasks," some sort of a header, right, and item 3 reads: "Work with ULT 220 at Branjevo." You agree, don't you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Are there any similarities between ULT 220, the type mentioned in this order, and the ULT that we saw being used in another document a while ago?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a similarity, the name of both types is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is this yet another ULT 220 that was dispatched to Branjevo on that day?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know at the time what type of machine this was or when it was dispatched, but we heard here this trial that there was a ULT 220 that was in the Jasenica quarry, and a while ago we saw that document in relation to ULT 220 belonging to Birac holding which is the Glinica company. So these might well have been two different pieces of machinery bearing the same name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If there is a daily order pursuant to which a machine is dispatched on a mission, does fuel come with that, the fuel required for that particular mission?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order should be as follows: This order should be written on the 16th, and it should contain a plan for these machines to do some work on the 17th as it reads, or there should be an attachment to this daily order, an addendum to cover the eventuality of these machines being used as an emergency. However, what we are looking at here is obviously exactly the other way around, someone got the machine, someone filled up, someone dispatched it to be used elsewhere; and then later on it was recorded as part of the daily order reflecting the fact that the machine was used for some work at a location. I'm no handwriting expert, but I'm not sure myself whether the handwriting is the same in the first part of the daily order and the bottom half where we see the tasks. One thing that I can say with certainty is the company commander signed the orders at a later stage and not when they were actually drafted because at the time he was somewhere in the Crni Vrh area.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any misgivings about the substance of these documents or just about the time they were signed?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He probably didn't even issue this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you perhaps tell what the reason would be for something like this to be recorded at all?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can make assumptions about what the reason might have been. Once the machine was used and everything that was done was carefully recorded, then it would only have been logical for this to be recorded by the engineering company. Who was it who told the commander or the clerk in the company to write something like this or this in particular, I really don't know. Nevertheless, in relation to ULT 220, that particular machine, I know that it wasn't used by the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you talking about the ULT 220 from this order or the one from the previous document that I showed you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about a ULT 220, and it's anyone's guess whether we're really looking at the first machine being mentioned or the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Going back to the previous document, we saw that on the 17th of July, 170 litres of fuel were issued with respect to this piece of machinery, and, if needed, we can go back to the document for confirmation. I do believe you saw that, did you not? Can you tell me whether the amount of fuel was recorded as fuel consumption of the brigade in the regular combat report?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fuel that was issued from the petrol station that day was issued by someone who did not particularly want to know what the fuel would be used for, but they had to record it. It would have been logical for something like this to be reflected in the documents as daily consumption in relation to whichever day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you expressed a desire to see what had become of those 360 litres of fuel. I would like to know show you a document that has been admitted in this trial. It's also on our list, 1D692. 1D692. If you look at the upper half of this document, you will see that this is an intercept, the 16th of July, 1995. We must focus on conversation number 662, that being the last conversation here. It was intercepted at 1355, a conversation between two unidentified males. Do you want to have back on your screen the conversation which Popovic purportedly requests fuel? That was three minutes later. That's how it was recorded, 1358. This conversation and let me read it because it's not particularly long one: "X: Says 90 litres now 100 litres. Y: Oh fuck it. X: We calculated it on the map, 200 kilometres in one direction and 200 in the other, I don't know. What have you decided? Y: I don't know. I'm thinking about coming here across Kotromanjici. X: Where is that? Y: That's over there, (town of Dobrun). I'm not sure what this parentheses is supposed to mean. X: That's the direction. Y: Yes, Veto is going to. He will be staying in Uzice for 15 days. X: I don't have that much fuel. I don't know. I'm thinking about telling this guy to put a little in for us as well, so when we go back, which way should we go back? Y: Well, if I have any problems we can at least deliver the old one. Well, I don't know if it's that far. X: Of course it is, I just looked at the map with the traffic policeman. I'll check with my guys if I'll be able to secure petrol, and if I do, we'll go together. Y: I called you to tell you. X: It's 450 kilometres further along." Tell me, does this conversation not indicate that this is some sort of a job, something being taken 450 kilometres from an already-determined route, and the people participating in this conversation need some fuel.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, this conversation is apparently not recorded from the very beginning because hardly would anyone start a conversation with 190 litres, 100 litres; however, I presume that this is about the transportation job that, according to this, should have gone via Visegrad all the way to Bruno [phoen] and Kotroman and further on to Uzice. So this is an entirely different direction compared to the Vlasenica-Zvornik direction. What this is all about, I honestly cannot tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Pandurevic, I would like now to go back to a portion of your evidence which relates to another intercept of a conversation that took place on the 22nd of September, 1995. Just a moment, please. It was at 1844, and that's Prosecution Exhibit 2391. I apologise, it's 2319. I think the most legible version is the one in B/C/S, which is version D whereas version A is in English. [In English] It is 2391. [Interpretation] That's 2391 D in B/C/S. Can we please go to the bottom of the document in B/C/S, it begins at the very bottom of the document and goes on, on the next page. I'm sure you remember this conversation, but let us remind ourselves, it took place on the 22nd of September, 1995, the time is 1844. Can we please look at the next page in B/C/S. I don't think it's necessary for me to read the whole conversation to you because it's already been read and entered into the transcript; however, can we confirm that the person marked as P, Popovic, is asking whether the fuel had arrived. He's also inquiring about Trbic, et cetera, and then he says, line third from the bottom, he says: "Could you please find out if it came, if it arrived. Call the gas station." Can we say that he wants to know whether fuel had arrived at the petrol station?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I will now ask you to look at regular combat report dated the 22nd September, 1995, that's 7D676.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: To clarify the record, could we get who the questioner thinks the "he" is because it's not clear from the record, and I think it's important he should put his case to who he's talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: May I remind you, Mr. Zivanovic, that the B/C/S version is under seal, and cannot broadcast it, okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that it is under seal, is it? The one before is under seal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's okay, it wasn't broadcast, don't worry. I was just drawing your attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: To clarify, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From this transcript, can you discern who the person marked P is?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A certain Popovic and a certain Nidzo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I think that this certain Popovic is clearly identified in the preamble to this conversation. If you don't remember --

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have this transcript in front of me, this intercept.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Never mind. Can we please now look at -- yes, here, it says --

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we now move to document 7D676, please. If we look at this regular combat report, the lower part on the very end of it -- can we please just scroll up the B/C/S version a little. I think that we can see that this report was dispatched at 1600-and-something hours. I wonder if you can help me with that; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We can also say that that was two or two and a half hours before the conversation that we saw a minute ago which took place at 1844?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we now look at item 6 of this report. If you can just zoom out the B/C/S version a little. This is a standard clause relating to the consumption of fuel and other things on that day, and it says that 397 litres of diesel was used up. However, I would like you to look at item 8 and it reads: "Requests: We request your approval for oil for four freight trucks which will be transporting troops to relieve units in the area of Kacar-Spiljanska Stena (area of responsibility of the 2nd Romanija Infantry Brigade.) The unit from the Bratunac Brigade will return using the same vehicles." Mr. Pandurevic, I've noticed that only in this particular combat report of all the ones that we have seen so far, there is a precise explanation of the reasons why an increased amount of fuel is being requested. In all other reports, it is just said that the requests are made based on the requests coming from the command. We can look at these other requests -- reports and see exactly what it is all about. Can you understand the reason why, in this particular report, we have specific reasons for requesting a certain amount of fuel?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will describe to you what the practice was in place relating to item 8 in this report. If a brigade was engaged in carrying out missions under the orders of the corps, outside of its defence zone, we would do our best to acquire additional amounts of fuel in order not to use our own fuel for the missions carried out in somebody else's zone. This is one of such instances, and it was not the only one. It happened on several occasions. If you want to establish a correlation between item 8 and the intercept, I can also tell you a few things about it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear what the counsel said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. The interpreters didn't hear you at all this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you repeat whatever you said. If it was a question, could you repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead, please. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'll go on. This is a new thing for me. If these two engaged in a conversation are people from the security organ that we think they are, in addition to clearly described jobs that they have, they are additionally engaged in logistics and operations duty like provision of fuel, transportation of units, et cetera. I find that to be surprising; therefore, the rules of service would have to be amended accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Wasn't your understanding that this conversation was probably having to do with prevention of theft?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The war lasted four years. This is another possibility, another mode of stealing fuel. However, this is nothing to do with theft and has nothing to do with security organs whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You were absent at the time?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But you were well informed that this was not a theft.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you tell me how do you know that this was a theft?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, we didn't hear what the counsel said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Zivanovic, the interpreters didn't hear what you said.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters are kindly asking the speakers not to overlap, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's a question of overlapping. It's a question of overlapping, so please allow a pause between question and answer and try to speak in the microphone. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And also I think the parties are assuming, without saying in the question or putting the case to the witness, who these people are. I think we've identified Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic, but there is, from the record we see a Nidzo Mihalic, so if there is someone -- they are assuming this is besides Nidzo Mihalic, I think it's incumbent upon them to say this otherwise we're guessing what they're talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It might be on Mr. McCloskey to do in his cross-examination to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Go ahead but please don't overlap and that applies to you and Mr. Pandurevic, and try to speak into the microphone which is not switched on at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I said that this was a suspicion.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic, and I would also kindly ask you when you see me waiting, it doesn't mean that I need an additional explanation of your question, I'm just waiting for the translation. As for your question, I asked you where this suspicion comes from.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that there was a document relating to the receipt of 5.000 litres of fuel on the 14th of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how this fuel was used up?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we now please look at 668, 7D668, please. I'm sorry, it's 7D669. Let us just note that this is the usual consumption of fuel and let us look at item 8 that I mentioned to you a short while ago. Can you please scroll down the B/C/S version. [In English] Another page. [Interpretation] Next page. [In English] I believe it is the third page of this document in B/C/S version. [Interpretation] Would you agree that item 8 in all regular combat reports is being formulated identically and it reads: Requests pursuant to the command organs request with the exception of the one that I showed you a while ago which was dated the 22nd of September?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this item was often phrased like this, but sometimes no requests like this were made by the command organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we please now go to 7D669. [In English] May we go back to the first page, please. [Interpretation] Can we now look at the fuel consumption for the 15th of September, D-2, 6.702 litres, I think. 6.702. It was 5.000 on the 14th; right?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I might as well take your word for it, but I don't know what document you're talking about. I know about a document dated the 14th mentioning 5 tonnes of fuel, but that wasn't for the Zvornik Brigade, it was for a very particular purpose; and it was by the commander of the Main Staff, if that's what you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is this fuel that never reached the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where it ended up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It reads here that on this day, the 15th of September, the day after, 5.000 litres of fuel came but you don't know where to, a total of 6.702 litres were used up. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is reflected here, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I can tell you why this was written and why so much fuel was used up; do you know why?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Please explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I will, as long as you don't know, but if you do, then perhaps you would like to explain this to us.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only assume why.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Part of the brigade went to the area covered by the 2nd Krajina Corps, a large amount of fuel was needed for that and I think if you look at the first part of the report, you will see that or perhaps the next combat reports if we look at it. Nevertheless, you see such a large amount of fuel was used up that followed the 5.000 litres that we talked about. Would that not give rise to suspicions that maybe there was some sort of malpractice at work here since such a large amount was used up, 6.702 litres?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If your illusion is to the 5 tonnes and then you mentioned the 6.702 litres, and you talk about malpractice, then someone used up these 6.702 litres to their own detriment, but I think you are right when you assume that the fuel was used for the purposes of the units that were dispatched to the Krajina area. In addition to this large amount of fuel, there are large amounts of ammunition being used up too; whereas as in item 1 and number 2 of this report, we don't see any major combat operations in progress.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please look at 7D670, I think that is the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The document is under seal, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters can't hear counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he's speaking to himself, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's the previous report, but if you look at the exceptional occurrences we can see that there were some casualties in the area covered by the 2nd Krajina Corps, which I think indicates that the Zvornik Brigade was there. It may have been in the previous report or the one before that, I might as well have a look and then you'll tell you. Nevertheless you will see again that now the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters could not hear the figure mentioned by counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear the figure that you mentioned, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You can see here that the consumption on that day was 1.930 litres of fuel?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pandurevic, do you perhaps see that for some reason, the security organs were monitoring this fuel shipment perhaps in a bid to prevent any malpractice? For example, that seems to have been the case on the 16th of July with those 500 litres.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see what it is that you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's not mentioned in the document, that's true.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's not mentioned and on top of that, I don't know what you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You don't understand my question about the risk of theft when major amounts of fuel are shipped; is that what you don't understand?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, generally speaking, this whole notion of fuel being stolen and all that, it's very difficult for me to get a handle on, at least from where I stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I fully understand what you are saying. Can we go back to where we left off, item 8 of the request. You see that the wording here is quite peculiar. It was explicitly requested that the purpose for this fuel be stated. Item 8 is quite differently worded, and there is a very specific explanation of what the fuel would be used for and this is entirely different from all of the other combat reports; do you not agree?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree. If you go back to the previous item, it also says that the Zvornik Brigade trucks would be bringing back soldiers from the Bratunac Brigade, which means they had to take them to Bratunac not to Zvornik. So in order to avoid using their own fuel for other people's business, we requested this amount of fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You weren't there at the time, were you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Again, you seem to really know the low down on what was going on with the fuel in those days.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at item 8 of that other report, and I'm not sure what the date is, it reads that a request was submitted for fuel. The change-over was probably supposed to take place on the following day. If you read between the lines and see theft, then your observation and your perception is different from mine, and I feel the need to apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What about this conversation that we've been talking about. Do you associate that conversation with the 14th September fuel or this other fuel shipment on the 22nd of September?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you insist, there is mention of Mr. Trbic in the other conversation, and then if we look at the order dated the 14th, the one dispatched by General Mladic, and pursuant to instructions on control over the security intelligence organs in the VRS, paragraph 5 says that the commander of the Main Staff or the chief of the security and intelligence sector may dispatch security officers on special missions. Therefore, in that order, General Mladic puts Trbic in charge of a mission like that, the mission being to look after the 5 tonnes of fuel and to keep records on how those 5 tonnes were used. Was there any theft involved in this process, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you believe that Mladic's order on the 14th was not carried out on the 22nd?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe either of these. I don't know when this was begun. I don't know when it was completed. I don't know who carried out the engineering work or indeed where.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Based on Trbic's name alone, because he's mentioned in this conversation, you associate him with the 14 September fuel.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked what my opinion was, and I am telling you that that is one way for me to see that conversation. My inference is not necessarily accurate although it strikes me as logical. It still doesn't mean that it's accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see any links between the conversation that we talked about, the 22nd September intercept, 1844, and the request that was dispatched only two and a half hours earlier? Do you see any links, for example, about whether fuel arrived?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. If you go back to that conversation, you will see that work was in progress and apparently there was no fuel at one point. So the other guy asks, Has any arrived in the meantime? And the respondent says he doesn't know. That is what Trbic is doing.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know they were mentioning work in progress. I don't know what exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the second time running, the interpreters haven't heard your question, neither have we. I mean the problem is because you need to cooperate a little bit better, I'm sorry I have to do this. The problem is that you are almost the only one who forgets about the microphone and speaks directly at the witness, so I mean there is no reason for that because I think Mr. Pandurevic and the microphone is exactly in the same line between Mr. Pandurevic and yourself; so you speak in the microphone, you will help us a great lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Pandurevic, you saw the 22nd September conversation that was quoted back in 1995. Did you see anyone mention the fact that someone had run out of fuel? If you want, we can go back to that conversation, that's 9321 -- or 2391.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, bring it back, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: 2391. I think we can move on to page 2 in the B/C/S because page 1 is only the beginning, but let's make sure we don't skip anything. [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sure, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at this bit where it says M: And then M says: "I am not up to date on that, fuck it." And then B says, "Does Trbic know, is he there, someone?" "M: He left. P: He is working on that, right? M: Yes, he is working, but I think he said that not much work will be done today," which means that worked had stopped on that day or was about to stop probably because of the fuel, and that's why he wants to know whether any fuel has arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. As far as I know, Trbic was busy doing something else. Why do you think that this is anything to do with fuel or any business that was fuel-related?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the people taking part in this conversation associate Trbic's work with fuel. It is obvious that the sort of work he is doing depends on fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How come that is so obvious to you that his work depends on fuel, based on what?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's based on this exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, but the person marked as P, Popovic, is he asking about Trbic or is he asking about fuel?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is asking whether -- THE INTERPRETERS: The interpreters did not hear counsel or witness because counsel overlapped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, Mr. Pandurevic, you are causing a lot of distress for the interpreters who couldn't follow because you overlapped, so we need to go back. Where should we start from. Should we start from line 7 again, page 22, let me read: "Excuse me," this is your question, "but the person marked as P, Popovic, is he asking about Trbic or is he asking about fuel?" Now, your answer, please, Mr. Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this conversation we can see that P established contact with Nidzo, and he's asking him if fuel had arrived. Nidzo doesn't have that information. P then asks whether Trbic knows anything about this, and then they go on to mention that Trbic was doing some work but that not too much work would be done on that day. Probably P was aware of what Trbic was doing and probably he had dispatched fuel to him and fuel had arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, did he send fuel to Trbic or to the brigade? Was that fuel intended for the brigade or for Trbic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this conversation took place between the assistant for the logistics of the Drina Corps and the assistant for logistics of the Zvornik Brigade, I would understand that the fuel is part of the regular tasks carried out by the brigade and the logistics department. During my whole career and my experience in war, I never received fuel for my brigade through security lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was this fuel sent down the security line?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To put it plainly, these two men are after some fuel. They don't know its whereabouts but they need it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe they were bent on stealing it.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't go that far to accuse them of such a thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. At any rate, you are not able to deduce from this conversation, and it doesn't occur to you that this is -- this conversation relates to paying attention to the fuel relating to the requests mentioned earlier; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these are poor counter-intelligence methods if they are operating in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pandurevic, so far, I haven't asked you anything about counter-intelligence method of work because you said you were not familiar with that; however, since I see that you are quite familiar with that, tell me, is one of the duties of security organs to provide protection against sabotage or rather covert enemy activities within the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what we used to call in the SFRY an internal enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: So you were familiar with the regulations governing security activities concerning enemies from within? They were similar?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: As I understood you when you gave evidence, you said that when you arrived at the brigade, you were not at all familiar with those rules and regulations that you didn't know how security organs were used. Can you correct me? Am I right when I say that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not that ignorant.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Based on your understanding of the notion of an enemy within, could anyone undermine the army by stealing large amounts of fuel during the war? Can such person be deemed as an internal enemy? How do you perceive that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I see them as ordinary thieves.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If such person holds such a position in the army that allows them to take large amounts of fuel and abuse their position, you would still deem them to be ordinary thieves; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. An internal enemy was a completely different thing in the communist era. Those were all those who were opposed to the socialist order, even if there existed none, they should have been created.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What was the situation in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no such category as internal enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What about sabotage activities?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sabotage activities are activities that are planned and organised either by individuals or groups within VRS units with the aim of undermining combat readiness of the units. It can be carried out in a variety of ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: So if we have a group of individuals taking for themselves such vitally important fuel and thereby weakening the units of the VRS, is that a sabotage activity as you see it?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is possible, but it doesn't have to be the case always.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If it is possible, would that be the jurisdiction of security organs?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is their duty to keep an eye on that and if possible to prevent such activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I will consult my client, and I believe it is time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll have a 25-minute break now. Thank you. How much longer do you think you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I will consult my client, and let you know after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Twenty-five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm almost done, but I need just five minutes more, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We grant you four. Let's proceed. It took three hours instead of two, so let's proceed and finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: General, can you please look once again at Exhibit 302 that's the work log that you gave evidence on. Can you tell me who usually opens such a work log?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An organ with the traffic service.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: So that applies to this work log as well?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To all of them, even the form has been designed by the traffic service.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Or the transportation service, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at the bottom of this document where we can see somebody's signature, can you tell us what this signature signifies?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have here line 1 and line 2. Line 2 is the signature of an officer from the transportation organ, and in this specific case, it was signed by a man called Pantic, which means that he was responsible for issuing this work log. Line 1 should contain the signature of the officer from the unit where this work log is being used.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just one more question. At the top of this document, we can see a stamp. Is that normally the brigade stamp put in when the work log is opened?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the stamp of a military post. I am not sure that a stamp is required here or should a stamp only be put at the very end of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: My last question: These vehicle work logs are not opened for privately-owned vehicles that are not used for official purposes?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If someone specifically requested from the transportation service or the technical service to be issued fuel, in order for them to have proof and certificate of issuing fuel, they have to open a new work log and to enter the quantity of the fuel issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And here at the bottom, we see the figure 270 litres. Can you see that, that that is the usual quantity and the usual consumption?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a total quantity of fuel and the actual consumption as per norm, this is a rather precise figure for this type of machine that works by the hour, and it was very difficult to fit all this together but I believe that this machine -- excuse me, this machine had already come with a certain amount of fuel in its tank and that it reached the Zvornik Brigade in such a condition; and then on the 15th of July, 60 litres were added to it, whether it happened before or after the work was done, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This machine had arrived from Birac Holding company; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is exactly what I said in examination-in-chief, that is what Jokic told Obrenovic and the way these machines were taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And this machine came from the holding with a tank filled with fuel?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course nobody pushed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As you know my name is John Ostojic, and I'm here with Mr. Predrag Nikolic and we represent Mr. Ljubisa Beara. Sir, earlier at the start of your testimony, we were kind of challenged by your counsel and you, I suppose, to put our case to you; and let me start off by telling you off the bat that I do not believe, with all due respect, you on several issues. I think what you've testified to is a post facto construct in order to create a defence, a failed defence, which was used by the Krstic defence team as well as the Blagojevic Jokic defence team, and you're not surprised at all by our position; would I be correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would first kindly ask you not to speak so loudly. You are too close to me and I'm hearing both your voice and the voice of the interpreter, and I find it difficult to follow both. As far as your question whether I'm surprised by that position of yours, knowing your views and after following this trial, I'm not very much surprised.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pandurevic, I will try to keep my voice down or move the mike a little lower. I don't mean to yell at you, but we are close to one another here. Sir, I also just want to tell you that I don't agree on a number of issues and so there's no surprises, I'm going to highlight some of them and we'll have a discussion about them in the next few days. For example, these aren't an exclusive list but, for example, I don't agree with your position or your theory on absence of commander and this senior officer issue that you raised. I don't agree with you on your zone of defence versus zone of responsibility. I don't agree with you with the issue of POWs and whether they are "my POWs," or Main Staff POWs. I don't agree with you about the contents of the purported conversations you had with Mr. Obrenovic on the 16th, 17th, and 18th of July, 1995. Further, I don't agree with you for the reasons you gave us as to the opening of the corridor. And also, on small issues, I don't agree with you on the issue that you raised with respect to brotherhood and unity as well as your tenure in Slovenia. So if I can begin first, because as I'm sure you noticed, I always like to have a time-line of certain events, so can you tell us at the outset when did you first prepare to retrace or recount your actions relating to July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hope, Mr. Ostojic, that you agree with my full name, if nothing else. I was a participant in those events and I do recall a lot of them, even without the documents that I had seen post festum here in The Hague. As I said, my decision to testify in this trial was made on the very first day I reviewed the indictment. More than two years ago, I told my defence team about the facts that I have knowledge about and that I stated here in examination-in-chief. It was up to them to put it in a proper legal form and refer them to proper legal paragraph, and I don't agree with you about what you don't agree with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, when was the -- did you ever have an occasion to talk to the Krstic defence team before you were indicted?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: On how many occasions?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't say. Twice, perhaps three times, no more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the trial was in progress already, therefore, I can't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As I mentioned to you, I'm just trying to establish a time-line. We know that you met with Eileen Gilleece on October 2nd, I belive, 2001. Prior to that, in May 2001, is when the Krstic trial judgement was rendered; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll --

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who was it that I met in May?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll break it down. I'm sorry. In October of 2001, you met with the OTP investigator Eileen Gilleece; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Several months before that, in May of 2001 is when the Krstic trial judgement was rendered. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware of the fact that there was a judgement, but I was not aware of the substance of that judgement.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And immediately prior to that, I think on April 15th, 2001, your Chief of Staff at the time July 1995, Dragan Obrenovic, was arrested April 15th, 2001; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you know the exact time-line and all the dates, I have no reason not to trust you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that. And I do have that little bit of time-line down. But what I'm curious to know is when you met with the Krstic defence team in Belgrade, when was it? Was it in 1999 before or after your meeting with Dragan Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said, I met Mr. Petrusic in his office two or three times during the Krstic trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, help me with that. Was it before or after your meeting with Dragan Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I think I met Dragan Obrenovic in Belgrade after his statement to the OTP, which I believe occurred in 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about the Blagojevic-Jokic defence team, did you ever meet with them?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about Dragan Obrenovic's defence team, did you ever meet with them?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Who is the first person you ever shared this purported conversation that you had and the contents of it regarding July 16th, 1995 to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are many things that happened. I didn't single out this date as something special to tell anyone. I told my own lawyers as I said over two years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Have you talked to anyone else about your activities or conduct in July of 1995 other than that which you've shared with us here? I mean your lawyers, the Krstic defence team, Obrenovic, and other than family, sir?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for what happened in 1995, more specifically July 1995, and my own involvement, I discussed this with my defence team, with Ms. or Mrs. Gilleece according to that report and the way we interpreted to that report here. I spoke to Obrenovic as events were unfolding. In addition to that, I never shared with anyone the details of my involvement at the time. There were general conversations about things that happened at the time but in a general way.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about one month before your meeting with the OTP and Ms. Gilleece, did you have a meeting with Mr. Mijatovic to discuss your involvement in July of 1995? Do you remember that at all?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used to see Mr. Mijatovic. I saw him from time to time. We did not go into any details. I think he mediated on one occasion in establishing contact with Semso Muminovic, he gave me his phone number, so that I could then go on and phone him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And did you, in fact, call Mr. Muminovic on September 5th, 2001, to discuss the issues of Srebrenica a month before your meeting with the OTP.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please in the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember the exact order in which these things happened, but I think that my meetings with the OTP have nothing to do with my previous conversation with Semso Muminovic. I think I spoke to him once over a mobile phone and once I used a land line to call his private number at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Why in 2001, I'm curious to know, were you so anxious to talk to Semso Muminovic, to the OTP, to the Krstic defence team, if you hadn't even been indicted yet at that point?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke about some things that I knew about the indictments, there were suspicions at the time that there were secret indictments being prepared. I didn't know at the time whether I was one of the potentially indictees or not, but I was simply looking the to the progress of the Krstic trial. I didn't follow this in the media because there wasn't much in that way, and I didn't really hear much about this in my conversation with Mr. Petrusic. I wanted to speak to Mr. Muminovic in order to refresh his memory of our joint activities back then. There was a large-scale campaign in the media and otherwise that was in progress at the time. I was embarrassed to be publicly associated with certain events for which I did not consider myself responsible.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever get a letter from General Krstic while he was at the UNDU because he sent it to several Generals regarding his activity or actions relating to Srebrenica; were you one of the recipients of that letter?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I sent him a copy of my book, the fundamental doctrine on the defence of Republika Srpska, and then he sent back a letter to me less than a page long to thank me for sending him a copy of my book; and some exchange of purely private information such as health, that kind of thing, and that was the extent of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Then we'll move away from that. Did you at any point, sir, read the trial judgement in the Krstic case?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read it here in The Hague. The trial judgement but not the final one.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And obviously since you've read it, you know your name appears on it in several instances specifically relating to the events that we've discussed during your direct and through the entirety of this trial, does it not?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. But I did not stand indicted in that case and my role was seen in quite a different light at the time. I had realised that there were a number of things that were mis-inferred at the time and misconstrued as far as the activity of the Zvornik Brigade was concerned and my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, when you met with the Krstic defence team, did they share with you what their theory of defence was?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, those were brief meetings. I asked some questions about how the trial was going and what the atmosphere was like, what exactly was going on. Mr. Petrusic told me nothing about their defence strategy if that's what you're driving at.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Tell me when was the first time you learned that the defence of General Krstic was to shift the responsibility to the security organs, when did you first become aware of that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't learn about their intention to shift the responsibility to the security organs at all. There is a newspaper in Belgrade which brought some parts of the interview that he gave to the OTP. I read those portions that were published. In addition to that I knew nothing else -- or rather beyond that, I knew nothing about his appearance before this Trial Chamber or what he actually said.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I want to ask you just preliminarily a couple questions regarding the July 16th and July 17th purported conversations and the alleged contents of those conversations that you had with Obrenovic. Correct me if I am wrong, you believe that the contents of that conversation are important and, in fact, vital to your defence; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It isn't just that. There are a lot of things that I believe to be vital for my defence and I have addressed quite a number of these issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you have and we'll touch upon them, I'm sure, in the next couple of days. There was no reason, was there, sir, for you to hide the contents of that conversation with anyone; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such as who?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: From anyone, from let's say your lawyers, the OTP, other people that you met? It's something that you had no reason to hide.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told my defence team about that, and I did not discuss the details of what happened at the time with anyone else. This is just a single day, but there are a number, quite a number of other dates that are vital and that we have been talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pandurevic, I'm just focussing right now just on those particular conversations. We'll get into the other stuff, but for right now, I know there's other material that you believe is vital. And we'll try to get to that. My point is actually because this vital and important information that you had relating to this alleged conversation with Obrenovic and this supposed contents of that conversation, you would have disclosed it because it's the truth to just about anyone; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, do you have any information on me disclosing anything else such as something that I've been talking about in chief, for example, and throughout my entire evidence here?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's see if I can put my finger on it. How about if we take a look at 2D646, please. I know as we've all sat here for almost three years we've become very accustomed to learn these procedures and what 92 ter and 92 quater and 65 ter rules are. This, sir, as it's coming up on the screen is your filing of your 65 ter list and again it's 2D646, and we're going to go to page 13 because it summarises, in essence, your testimony that you're going to give in this case. Have you seen this document ever before?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I note from Mr. Haynes' comments yesterday even -- I'm just going to find this so I don't misquote it. On page 32 of yesterday's transcript, line 19 through 20 he states: "We are all creatures of our instructions and all the decisions we have to take have to be taken in consultation with Mr. Pandurevic." Did you consult with them regarding your summary about your testimony and the testimony of other witnesses?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly did. Nevertheless, if you look at our pre-trial brief, the 65 ter, and the theories about my evidence, this is far more detailed than the overall theories that you had in your pre-trial brief. I remember certain objections being raised. You see that 18 hours were planned and what we actually ended up with was 30. I consulted with my lawyer on this, but, please, Mr. Haynes proceeds in the following way. He hears me out. He listens to me on -- as far as professional aspects of my work were concerned. He got all the facts from me, but it was his call eventually to determine how things would proceed in a purely legal sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that, and I'm not looking for you to explain that to me, but in any event, thank you. What I'm looking at here is your 65 ter summary. If we turn to page 15 which is the third page of this document that is in e-court, and it's not in B/C/S, so I'm grateful that you do know English. In the third bullet point, and this is, as it's being brought up, is really a rundown of what you're going to testify. It's chronological with dates and basically some background information but in the -- as you can see from the first bullet point on that page, and then the second bullet point talks about the 15th of July then we go to the next bullet point which talks about the 16th of July; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The bullet point right underneath that kind of talks about the 16th and 17th. Nowhere -- and you can look through the whole document which you've already seen, I'm sure -- nowhere in the 65 ter summary does it mention that you had a conversation purportedly with Mr. Obrenovic on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, you are suggesting that the summary contains nothing on the conversation that occurred on the 16th. Am I getting you right, the conversation with Dragan Obrenovic, that's what you're saying; right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And the 17th just to make it go a little quicker.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there's only a small portion in relation to the 17th, but I can't see the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll give you the next pages because the next page is it continues about the 17th, and then we go on to the period of the 18th through the 21st; but my focus is really on those two conversations that allegedly occurred with you and Mr. Obrenovic on the 16th and 17th. And I'm lumping them together just for the sake of trying to speed up this minor point. But if it's true, Mr. Pandurevic, that you shared this with people, and it's the truth, and it's something that there was no reason to hide it, why wouldn't it appear on a summary of the testimony you were going to offer this past month? Because certainly if you keep reading the conversation you had with Obrenovic on the 18th is expressly stated there. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The print is too small, that's probably what it says, but I'm not sure what it says exactly if it claims that there was a conversation on 23rd because there was another one on the 23rd that actually took place. I'm not sure if it's part of the summary or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's not. But really I'm just focussing on trying to understand or if you can reconcile for me why was it your decision to omit or not to place the contents of this purported conversation with Mr. Obrenovic on the 16th and 17th of July; but you chose only to share with us and the Court and the Prosecution the contents of a purported conversation on the 18th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the 65 ter summary was drawn up, I had a meeting with my defence team. We agreed on a witness list and generally on the substance of the summary. This was done and a copy was forwarded to me. I was not involved in the actual production of these points here. It was something that was done by the defence team. I consider it hence to be part of our defence strategy.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I could appreciate that given your comments about our team and our filings. But let me ask you this, I suggest to you, sir, that your defence team didn't know about the conversations you purportedly had with Mr. Obrenovic on the 16th and 17th, and it didn't include it; and it was merely as I said in my opening introduction it was construct by you and you looked at some of the evidence; and you fit this neatly in a package in order to prepare your defence; wouldn't I be right about that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not right, I disagree. At the outset, you were saying that I had many contacts even before this with the Krstic defence team and something to do with the Blagojevic-Jokic trial and all sorts of conversations, and that I had already drawn up this construct at the time; but now you're saying something that means quite the opposite. I informed my defence team, and they were the ones that took the decision for this summary to take the present form.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll switch gears a little bit here, Mr. Pandurevic. You told us briefly that you received your doctorate degree; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sociology.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Where did you receive that doctorate degree?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: East Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And when, please?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe late June 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And what was the theme of your dissertation or thesis that you defended or passed with high honours, I think you shared with us?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fundamental sociological hallmarks of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, earlier in your testimony, you spoke about brotherhood and unity or perhaps even in the opening remarks by your counsel. And then you told us that you were in Slovenia at the beginning of the war, and you even meanings mentioned that you spoke Slovenian; and now isn't it true that while you were in Slovenia, you did not assimilate with the people there? And assimilate is, I think, the technical word that sociologists should know?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we are looking at something that we call cooperation processes, assimilation and aculturation are two such processes. I was subject to aculturation, which means accepting the norms and the culture of life in your environment. I did not assimilate to the degree of compromising my own original identity or precisely the core of what made up my own ethnic background.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I looked up the word assimilate, and it actually says it's "to absorb into the culture or mores of a culture or group." A little bit different of what you said in terms of the definition of that word versus another one; and in fact, while you were at the JNA in Slovenia, you continued to maintain your Serbian nationalism; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what you mean when you say Serbian nationalism. I was an ethnic Serb, that was my nationality back then and it still is.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And are there certain attributes of a Serbian national?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Serb?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's it?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what you mean by "attribute."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll give you your quote because you used that phrase in a minute, but first let me lay a little foundation. Do you remember giving an interview to, I think, either a television show or a newspaper called Srna?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have got to give you a hand with that. Srna was a news agency and there was the Serbian radio and TV; and yes, an interview with me was published for that TV station, an interview conducted in Zvornik. I don't remember the exact date, but I know that it was summertime.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Maybe I can help jog your memory. Do you know that it was with a producer or a journalist by the name of Risto Djogo?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of that programme, by chance?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My guest, his truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you were Mr. Djogo's guest and you were talking about your truth, right, at that interview?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was answering his questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now you gave us the approximate season of the interview, how about the year, when was that interview conducted, what year?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly 1994, but I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's look at it, if we can, and it's 2D638. Sir, it's page 4 in B/C/S that I'm just going to point out and it's page 3 in English of this exhibit. I think that's the start of your interview with him if I'm not mistaken, but you are certainly free to look at the first several pages if you like. Just tell me, is that the interview we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is probably a transcript of the actual recording.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It doesn't have the year. At the time the Prosecution was not helpful at all with providing us with the year of that although they tried. Sir, I want to just direct your attention if I can to the next two pages and just to get this issue about whether you assimilated with the Slovenians and what are the attributes of a Serbian national. If we can go to page 5 in the B/C/S and the English version; and I believe the B/C/S on page 5 is the last paragraph, so if we can perhaps highlight that for you. The journalist there as you can read for yourself asks you if you've learned Slovenian and then you answer and you say: "Yes, I did. I spoke Slovene very well, and I integrated. But I did not assimilate to use a technical term. I kept all the attributes of a Serbian national." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I would still answer the question the same way. But let me tell you, you gave a definition of assimilation a while ago, but one of the forms of assimilation is aculturation. I was subjected to that particular process, and that was fine by me; but I could at no point in time declare myself to be a Slovene. The best way to have myself accepted by the others was by being what I was. I was spending all of my time amongst Slovenes in a Slovene environment going to conferences, going to political rallies, doing sports with them and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And at that time, sir, when you were there, I think it was 1991, you were with the JNA. Yugoslavia, as it was at that point, had not yet fallen apart, if you will. Were you considering yourself a Serbian national or a Yugoslav given that you were in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you are an American national, and it's probably easier for you to understand nationality as citizenship and then ethnicity which is a different thing. I think the original citizenships in Yugoslavia were the republican one and the federal one. I had that of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the SFRY. There is nationality, and there is citizenship if you like, and ethnicity and these are different things.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's talk a little bit about your rank, and I'm very impressed with that which you have achieved both professionally, militarily, as well as your schooling, sir. From 1982 to 1995, a period of approximately 13 years, you achieved seven ranks in the military hierarchy; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that is what your calculation appears to indicate, then it must be right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It does. But I'm going to go through the ranks anyway. The lowest rank which is a 2nd Lieutenant, then you went from that rank to a Lieutenant, then to a Captain, then to a Captain 1st Class then to a Major, then to a Lieutenant-Colonel, then to a Colonel. I stopped at 1995, I know you have other ranks, you were a Major-General as well as a General in the Army of Yugoslavia, but I'm limiting you to 1995. Those are seven ranks in a course of 13 years that you achieved; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
